premises: Oxygen impurities in HfNbTaTiZr act as scattering centers that reduce electron mean free path.
At low temperatures (0–200 K), oxygen defects dominate electron scattering and cause residual resistivity.
At high temperatures (300–1200 K), both phonon and defect scattering are significant.
Conventional analytical models assume defect-free crystals and thus overestimate conductivity.
Incorporating oxygen-induced defect scattering into a computational model will improve conductivity predictions.
